blocks.text: **Tilde makes everyday objects you can tap or scan.** Hold your phone to one, or point its camera at the code, and your phone does something useful: it saves a contact, joins the Wi-Fi, opens a link, books a meeting. You print them yourself, then put what you like on each with the Tilde app.

items.text: **Cards:** the Tilde Card, a business card with a QR code on the front and an NFC sticker inside.
**Fobs:** coins and tags for your keys, in Base and Premium, and the Special Edition: Retro handheld.
**Home & desk:** the sticky note, the calendar and the grocery list for the fridge, the Wi-Fi coaster, the Tilde Stand and the Stand Mini.
**The app:** Tilde for Android, which writes what each one opens, and puts your card on your phone.

blocks.text: **Print a few, tag everything.** Any phone reads them; the app writes them. Tilde is Android only for now, and your iPhone reads every tag.
How every Tilde works (shared by every entry below)

items.text: **Scan:** any phone’s camera reads a printed code. No app needed.

**Tap:** an NFC sticker sits inside, under the tap icon. Hold the back of the phone flat on the icon, within 1–2 cm. `[Thomas: say where on an iPhone (near the top) and on most Android phones (near the camera or mid-back)? No source documents it for iPhones, so a test would settle it.]`
sub: **iPhone XS or newer:** reads a tap with the screen on, with no app and no setting. A link comes up as a notification. Not while Camera or Wallet is open.
**iPhone 7 to X:** open the NFC reader in Control Center first.
**Android:** NFC must be on, and the phone unlocked. A link opens. A contact card offers to save it. Guest Wi-Fi offers Connect.

items.text: **Write:** the sticker can be rewritten any time, through the plastic.
sub: **Android:** Tilde for Android’s **Write a sticker** (on the Cards tab in 1.3.0). It writes a link, your contact card, or your guest Wi-Fi.
**iPhone:** Tilde is Android only for now, and your iPhone reads every tag. To write a link from an iPhone, use the free NFC Tools app.

items.text: **What iPhones do with what’s on a sticker:**
sub: **A contact card:** in 1.3.0, a tap opens a contact page with Save contact (it needs internet on the iPhone). `[depends on T1–T4]` If they fail, an iPhone scans your phone’s code to save it.
**Guest Wi-Fi:** an iPhone joins by scanning a Wi-Fi code, never from a tap. The Wi-Fi page that a tap opens needs `wifi-page` and W1 `[depends on T-WF1–T-WF4]`.

items.text: **What fits on a sticker:** a link fits any NTAG213, 215 or 216 sticker. A full contact card needs room: Android offers to save it only if it fits (NTAG216 holds the most).
**Anything on a sticker or a printed code is public:** anyone who taps or scans it can read it. Write only what you’d put on a poster.

blocks.text: Get the app (every entry’s “Get the app”)
**Tilde for Android:** download the APK from GitHub releases, with the install steps (Android 8.0 or newer). It’s free, open source (MIT) and needs no account.

items.text: **Version:** 1.3.0, released this week as the GitHub APK (the app agent prepares it; Thomas OKs the push). Until then the APK is 1.2.0, and the 1.3 lines here (the Cards tab, the contact page) wait for it.

**Printing:** the printer pauses for the sticker, so it prints in a single print and comes out one solid piece.
**Save my contact:** hand it over; they scan or tap.

**WhatsApp:** a tap opens a chat with you.
